one_line: A battle-hardened Gondwana queen and the cultured Sultan of Malwa, facing off along the forested hill frontier of mid-16th century central India.

appearance.age_look: Both appear around their early 30s, athletic but not bulky; Durgavati with a rider’s wiry strength, Baz Bahadur with a refined yet capable build.
appearance.face: Durgavati has an oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes with a steady, resolute gaze, a straight nose, and a faint scar at her left eyebrow; default expression calm but intensely focused. Baz Bahadur has a slightly longer face with a lighter brown complexion, neatly trimmed mustache and short beard, expressive dark eyes that shift between contemplative and wary, with a composed, almost regal default expression.
appearance.hair: Durgavati’s hair is long, black, parted in the middle and drawn back into a thick braid that falls between her shoulder blades, wrapped at the end with a thin red cloth; she wears a simple dark green cloth headband beneath a narrow, gold-edged turban band that seats her small tiara-like diadem. Baz Bahadur’s hair is black, cut to just above the shoulders, straight and neatly combed back under a domed, emerald-green Malwa-style turban with a narrow gold band and a single white feather pinned slightly to the right.
appearance.costume: Durgavati wears a practical yet regal Deccan–Gondwana-inspired warrior queen outfit: a long-sleeved, thigh-length red cotton angarkha (cross-wrapped tunic) with a subtle gold floral block print and side tie knots, belted with a sturdy brown leather girdle; over it, she wears a fitted, sleeveless, dark forest-green quilted cotton armor vest with vertical stitching and small brass studs, cut high at the neck and flaring slightly at the hips. Her lower garment is a deep-indigo, narrow-pleated cotton lehenga-style skirt that tapers enough to ride easily, with a simple gold border near the hem, worn over plain off-white churidar trousers that wrinkle neatly at the ankles. A mustard-yellow cotton dupatta with a thin red border is draped from her left shoulder across her torso and tucked into her belt, trailing behind slightly to read as a battle-sash. She wears modest gold stud earrings, a small red bindi, a single thin gold necklace, and several slender bangles on her right wrist, but all kept minimal to suggest practicality; her feet are in brown leather riding shoes with slightly upturned toes. Baz Bahadur wears a refined Malwa court-warrior ensemble: a long, ankle-length, emerald-green silk jama (robe) with wrap-over front, fitted sleeves to the wrist, and a flared skirt, patterned subtly with darker green floral motifs; the neckline, cuffs, and front opening are edged with thin gold piping. Around his waist he wears a wide, dark maroon cloth kamarband (sash) with faint stripes, into which his weapon scabbard tucks. Over the jama he has a sleeveless, light-steel-colored mail-and-plate style torso coat rendered in quilted textile form for safety: visually evoking lamellar but clearly padded cloth, with small rectangular metal plates hinted beneath, hem reaching just above the knee. His trousers are slim off-white churidar, and his footwear is a pair of dark brown leather mojari with slightly curved toes. He wears a simple gold ring on his right hand and small, understated gold hoop earrings, emphasizing noble status without excess flash.
appearance.signature: Durgavati carries a long, slightly curved steel tulwar with a brass hilt and disc pommel, sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard hanging from her belt on the left, while Baz Bahadur carries a similarly elegant tulwar with a darker steel blade and a richly inlaid dark-maroon-and-gold scabbard tucked into his sash on his left side; both are often shown with their right hand resting lightly on the hilt to emphasize mutual readiness and respect as opposing commanders.

ref_desc: Rani Durgavati has an oval medium-brown face, sharp dark eyes, black braided hair, red angarkha, green quilted armor vest, indigo skirt, mustard dupatta and brown shoes with a brass-hilt tulwar, while Baz Bahadur has a lighter brown face, short beard, green turban, emerald jama, quilted armor coat, off-white churidar and maroon-sheathed tulwar.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two opposing mid-16th century central Indian leaders standing side by side: on the left Rani Durgavati, an athletic Gondwana queen with an oval medium-brown face, sharp dark eyes, a faint scar at her left eyebrow, long black hair in a single braid wrapped at the end with red cloth and held by a dark green headband and narrow gold-edged diadem band, wearing a long-sleeved thigh-length red cotton angarkha with subtle gold floral print, over it a fitted sleeveless forest-green quilted cotton armor vest with brass studs, a deep-indigo narrow-pleated skirt over off-white churidar trousers, a mustard-yellow dupatta draped from left shoulder across her torso and tucked into a brown leather belt, modest gold jewelry, brown leather riding shoes, and a long slightly curved steel tulwar with brass hilt in a dark brown scabbard hanging from her belt; on the right Baz Bahadur, a refined Malwa sultan with a lighter brown face, neat mustache and short beard, expressive dark eyes, black hair to just above the shoulders, wearing a domed emerald-green turban with a gold band and a single white feather, an ankle-length emerald-green silk jama with darker green floral motifs and gold piping, a wide dark maroon kamarband, a sleeveless light-steel-colored quilted mail-and-plate-inspired torso coat over the jama, off-white churidar trousers, dark brown leather mojari shoes, subtle gold earrings and a ring, and a curved tulwar with darker steel blade in a maroon-and-gold scabbard tucked into his sash; show them front and slight three-quarter views in one image to clearly display face, hair, full costumes, footwear and the tulwars, with colors rich and saturated but historically grounded and the overall tone dignified and heroic.
